concerns.text: Task T012b instructs the implementer to 'stop when the cumulative dataset size approaches a substantial threshold.' This silently relaxes Spec FR-001 which mandates fetching commits for 'each PR' in the representative set. The task introduces an arbitrary truncation not authorized by the spec, violating the requirement to fetch the full dataset for the selected repos.

Tasks T019b-d define a manual human workflow (T019b: 'Open this file... manually review') and T019d allows proceeding with 'UNVALIDATED' status if human data is missing. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires results to be reproducible by re-running code on a fresh runner without manual intervention. The task list fails to provide an automated fallback (e.g., synthetic mock data generation) required to satisfy FR-011 in an automated CI environment.

Tasks T026a (Standard MWU) and T026b (Stratified MWU) are both implemented without a clear decision criterion for which result constitutes the primary finding. Spec FR-006 mandates a 'Mann-Whitney U test' (singular). The Plan introduces a 'Stratified' extension, but the tasks do not specify which test result populates the final report, risking a silent relaxation of the primary hypothesis test requirement or an unapproved scope expansion.

Task T018c triggers a 'limitation statement' in the report if data quality is <95%. Spec SC-003 defines 95% as a system success threshold, but FR-012 (the only requirement for a limitation statement) is strictly tied to the false-negative rate >10%. This task conflates a system health check with the specific research limitation logic, potentially injecting non-spec-mandated text into the final report.

Task T023a requires excluding data from repos in `excluded_repos.txt`. While logically sound, the task description does not explicitly reference the specific edge case handling in Spec 'Edge Cases' (skipping repos with <50 PRs). More critically, if T014 (which generates this file) fails or is skipped, T023a has no defined fallback, potentially violating the robustness required by the spec's edge case handling.
